method: Post-evaluation diagnosis only; no new candidate outputs or gate edits; original judgments unchanged.

false_blocks.explanation: The outage lasted ... and service was restored by restarting ... uses an outage-duration clause plus passive restoration. No incident production supports that whole sentence; facts and pins are valid. This is a valid clean paraphrase, not a fact_mismatch.

The service was down ... and recovered when engineers restarted ... uses down/recovered when rather than an available incident grammar production. Trusted duration and component are correct; full matching abstains.

The application was offline ... before engineers restored service ... differs from the before production at offline versus unavailable. No synonym normalization exists; valid facts and the recovery relation do not overcome the full-match failure.

contaminated_control.contradictory_caveat: There is no mention of specific downtime details

original_review.reviewer: Codex assistant semantic review; not independent human adjudication; no grading inference calls
original_review.notes: Retains the 92-minute duration and database restart recovery, but invents database failure as the cause and states there is no mention of specific downtime details despite the exact duration in the source. Strict completion fails the preregistered no-contradictory-incident-fact condition; core facts are separately recorded as present. Unsupported cause makes this contaminated even if a reviewer treats the vague denial as non-contradictory, so it is not a clean-correct false-block candidate.
